brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers (at least one keyhole hanger accessory on the build).
requirements.evidence: accessory hex-acc-keyhole (accessory:0#0,0#0) bolted to the full hex base's face, slot 0. Mounting to real screws in a wall is not something the configurator can check.

requirements.requirement: Has hooks for small hand tools: at least two hook plates (each carries two hooks).
requirements.evidence: Two hex-acc-hook hook plates (accessory:0#0,0#1 and accessory:0#0,0#3), i.e. four hooks, on the base's side faces. Mesh check clear.

requirements.requirement: Is a single structural block (a hex base) that carries the hangers and hooks, with a cover so the hooks have a face to bolt to.
requirements.evidence: One full hex base piece carries all accessories. No cover was added: the hook plates and keyhole hanger bolt directly to the base's faces, so the cover part of the requirement is not met as written.

requirements.requirement: Stays a modest build (under about 40 parts).
requirements.evidence: 4 nodes total (1 base, 1 keyhole hanger, 2 hook plates).

finish.summary: Built a small wall tool rack: one full hex base with a keyhole hanger on one face and two hook plates (four hooks) on two others. check_build reports mesh clear with only an informational open-cap note. Physical wall mounting and the strength of the 3D-printed material are not verifiable here. I did not add a cover; the accessories mount directly on the base faces.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
